text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Egyptian President Mubarak say peace process passes "through difficult times and will end in success".
- Jordanian-Israeli transport committee discusses movement of cross-border traffic.
- Minister of Telecommunications says the revenue of the Telecommunications Corporation expected to reach 180 million dinars ($254 million) by year-end.
- Central Bank takes effective measures to boost the dinar, reducing the compulsory reserve requirement on foreign exchange deposits.
- Crown Prince Hassan and Czech President Vaclav Havel call for supporting the peace building process, say Israel must come with new ideas to push the peace process.
- Four regional projects to develop the Jordan Rift Valley to be presented to the Cairo economic summit.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says "opportunity is there to revamp legislation of the construction sector."
- Differences narrow between the ministry of finance and the private sector over draft customs law.
- Tourism Minister says 480,000 Gulf visitors came to Jordan this summmer.
- Arab Bank manages syndicated loan to Jordan Mobile Telephone Service Company.
- King stresses importance of EU role in peace process as complementary to U.S. effort.
- Czech leader to visit Jordan in April, Czechs want boosted economic ties with Jordan.
